title: FitTrack Ad From Supplied Screenshots
tests: Uses supplied app screenshots faithfully in a finished landscape ad rather than inventing replacement screens.

faults.what: Both portrait screenshots are enlarged and severely cropped to fill the widescreen frame, hiding their headers and cutting off substantial UI content, including lower text.
The audio transcription reports audible 'La la la la la' vocals, contrary to the requested instrumental-only soundtrack.
The ending FitTrack title overlaps the workout content on a dark translucent rectangle rather than forming a clean, distinct end card.

judge.summary: The 10-second widescreen ad shows the screens in order and ends with FitTrack, but severe cropping and audible vocals require a redo.

must_haves.item: The final video is 10 seconds long and landscape 16:9.
must_haves.why: The supplied duration is 10 seconds, and the output frames are landscape 16:9.

must_haves.item: The supplied FitTrack home screenshot appears before the supplied workout screenshot.
must_haves.why: The early frames show the home screen's workout and sleep statistics; later frames show squats and push-ups from the workout screen.

must_haves.item: Both screenshots remain recognizable and readable, without invented replacement UI.
must_haves.why: The visible UI matches the supplied screenshots, but severe cropping removes the headers and much of each screen, with lower entries cut off.
FitTrack is clearly readable in the 8.8-second frame, despite the cluttered placement.

must_haves.item: An upbeat instrumental track is audible, with no voiceover.
must_haves.why: The sound transcription identifies 'La la la la la' vocals, so the soundtrack is not instrumental-only; the beat's mood cannot be established from the transcript.
